title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 146
paragraphs: Having so resolved, they reconciled their quarrels, and then first sent three men as spies to Asia. On arriving at Sardis, these men gathered information about the king's army, but were discovered. After being examined by the generals of the land army, they were being led off to their deaths. Their death had been decreed — but Xerxes, on being informed of this, found fault with the generals' decision and sent some of his spear-bearing bodyguards, with orders to bring the spies before him if they were still alive. They found them still alive and brought them into the king's presence. Xerxes, having ascertained for what purpose they had come, commanded the spearmen to take them around and show them the whole army, both infantry and cavalry, and when they had had their fill of looking at it, to let them go unharmed to whatever country they wished.
